newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SMH has no fear of hostile bid - Hayek.
newsitem.headline: SMH has no fear of hostile bid - Hayek.

text.p: Swiss watchmaker Ste Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horlogerie SA (SMH) chief Nicholas Hayek said he did not fear a hostile takeover even though his pool of allied shareholders no longer controls a majority of shares.

"The majority is no longer guaranteed. The pool still has around 40 to 42 percent," Hayek told Reuters. Hayek himself has a stake of around 30 percent in SMH, whose products range from luxury Omega watches to plastic Swatch timepieces.

The pool agreement -- first struck in 1985 and extended in 1992 -- expires on June 30, but allows members to decide whether to remain or not as of 1997. Some investors, including Stephan Schmidheiny, have already sold or reduced their stakes.
Swiss media have speculated about a possible unfriendly takeover by a foreign competitor, but Hayek said he was not concerned.
"I have absolutely no fear of a hostile takeover," he said, although he acknowledged SMH was "very coveted, especially by U.S. companies. Some giant firms want to work together with us".

Hayek said SMH would be able to defend itself against any hostile advances. Shareholders need board approval to have registered share stakes of more than three percent entered in the share registry, thus giving them voting rights, he noted.
"And if push comes to shove, enough friends would vote with us that we could easily get 55 percent," he said.
SMH and the Hayek Group also have enough funds to buy more shares, he said. "We only have to buy (a stake of) around ten to 11 percent to control a comfortable majority."
SMH shares were down 10 Swiss francs to 789 in a weaker market at 0935 GMT.
